utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Good afternoon, ladies and gentlemen. Could Madam Registrar call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. Case number IT-95-12-I, the Prosecutor versus Ivica Rajic, also known as Viktor Andric.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. For the sake of the record, could we have the appearances, please. For the Prosecution first.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honour. Good afternoon, Your Honour. Kenneth Scott for the Prosecutor and Josee D'Aoust also, and our case manager Lakshmie Walpita.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. And for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLUJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honour. My name is Zeljko Olujic. I'm Defence counsel for Mr. Ivica Rajic from the Republic of Croatia, Zagreb, and with me in the courtroom today is my colleague Doris Kosta, co-counsel in the case. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. We will proceed with the further appearance of the accused, Mr. Rajic, pursuant to Rule 50(B) and 62 of Rules of Procedure and Evidence. First of all, I would like to recall the procedural history of the case. The initial indictment against the accused was issued by the Prosecution on the 23rd of August, 1995, and confirmed on the 29th August 1995. International arrest warrants were issued against the accused. On 13 September 1996, the indictment was reconfirmed, and again international arrest warrants were issued against the accused. The accused was arrested in Croatia on 5 April 2003 and transferred to the Detention Unit of the International Tribunal on 24 June 2003. On the initial appearance held on 27 June 2003, the accused pleaded not guilty to all counts of the initial indictment. On 25 August 2003, the Defence filed a motion challenging the form of the indictment. In its response filed on 4 September 2003, the Prosecution announced that it would file a motion for leave to amend the indictment in the near future and requested the Trial Chamber to suspend its decision on the merits of the Defence motion until the amended indictment is filed. The Trial Chamber, therefore, decided not to take any decision before being seized with the Prosecution's motion for leave to amend the indictment. On 23 October 2003, the Prosecution filed a motion for leave to amend the indictment and the supporting material concerning proposed amended indictment. By the order issued on 12 January 2004, the Trial Chamber granted leave to the Prosecution to amend the indictment and declared that the Defence motion on the form of the indictment moot. The Defence was granted, in accordance with the understanding reached at the Status Conference held on 3 November 2003, 45 days from disclosure of the supporting material concerning the amended indictment in which to file a preliminary motion on the form of the amended indictment pursuant to Rule 72(A)(2) of the Rules. The amended indictment which is the subject of the hearing today was filed by the Prosecution on 14 January 2004. On 20 January 2004, the Prosecution informed the Trial Chamber that supporting material concerning the amended indictment has been provided to the Defence on 15 January 2004. At this stage, I would like to ask Mr. Rajic: Mr. Rajic, can you hear the proceedings in a language that you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Have you received the amended indictment against you in a language you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Did you have a chance to discuss it with your counsel?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Did your counsel explain to you in detail the contents of that indictment?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. You may sit down.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Pursuant to Rule 62(3) of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence, Mr. Rajic is called upon to enter a plea of guilty or not guilty on each count of the new indictment. He may do so either today or within 30 days from this further appearance. If he fails to enter a plea within the time limit, the Trial Chamber shall enter a plea of not guilty on his behalf. Mr. Rajic, are you prepared to enter your plea today?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: As you have read the amended indictment and discussed it with your counsel, do you wish the indictment to be read out, which is your right, or do you waive this right?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I waive the right. There's no need for the indictment to be read out.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the microphones please be adjusted. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: So my suggestion is that I will now repeat the charges brought against you, and I will then ask you whether you plead guilty or not guilty to the specific charge. Since the initial indictment has been replaced by the amended indictment, I will ask you to enter pleas with regard to all charges contained in the new indictment. Your answer in each case may be guilty or not guilty as the case may be. Do you understand that, Mr. Rajic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I do understand that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Are you ready to plea at this moment?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm ready.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Let's proceed. Count 1 charges you with wilful killing, a grave breach of the Geneva Conventions of 1949, punishable under Article 2(a), 7(1) and 7(3) of the Statute of the Tribunal. How do you plead; guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I plead not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Count 2 charges you with murder, a violation of the laws or customs of war, as recognised by Article 3(1)(a) of the Geneva Conventions, punishable under Articles 3, 7(1) and 7(3) of the Statute of the Tribunal. How do you plead; guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Count 3 charges you with inhuman treatment (including sexual assault), a grave breach of the Geneva Conventions of 1949, punishable under Articles 2(b), 7(1) and 7(3) of the Statute of the Tribunal. How do you plead; guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Count 4 charges you with outrages upon personal dignity, in particular, humiliating and degrading treatment (including sexual assault), a violation of the laws or customs of war as recognised by Article 3(1)(c) of the Geneva Conventions, punishable under Articles 3, 7(1) and 7(3) of the Statute of the Tribunal. How do you plead; guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Count 5 charges you with unlawful confinement of a civilian, a grave breach of the Geneva Conventions of 1949, punishable under Articles 2(g), 7(1) and 7(3) of the Statute of the Tribunal. How do you plead; guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Count 6 charges you with cruel treatment, a violation of the laws or customs of war, as recognised by Article 3(1)(a) of the Geneva Conventions, punishable under Articles 3, 7(1) and 7(3) of the Statute of the Tribunal. How do you plead; guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Count 7 charges you with appropriation of property, a grave breach of the Geneva Conventions of 1949, punishable under Articles 2(d), 7(1) and 7(3) of the Statute of the Tribunal. How do you plead; guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Count 8 charges you with plunder of public or private property, a violation of the laws or customs of war, punishable under Article 3(e), 7(1) and 7(3) of the Statute of the Tribunal. How do you plead; guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Count 9 charges you with extensive destruction not justified by military necessity and carried out unlawfully and wantonly, a grave breach of the Geneva Conventions of 1949, punishable under Articles 2(d), 7(1) and 7(3) of the Statute of the Tribunal. How do you plead; guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Count 10 charges you with wanton destruction of a city or devastation not justified by military necessity, a violation of the laws or customs of war, punishable under Articles 3(b), Article 7(1) and 7(3) of the Statute of the Tribunal. How do you plead; guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. You may sit down, please. May the registrar please take note that Mr. Rajic has pleaded not guilty to all counts of the new indictment. And the registrar will be instructed to fix a date for trial when appropriate. At this stage, are there any matters that the Prosecution wishes to raise?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: May it please the Court. Just as a matter of record, Mr. President, as you've already mentioned, the supporting material did -- was sent is out to counsel on the 15th of January, and I believe that all should be in good order. I've not had any indication from counsel that there's been any problems with that material. I do have today, and will hand to counsel today -- there were four translations that were missing in -- from English into B/C/S and were not available at the time in that binder -- or bundle, I should say, on the 15th, but I have those today, and I think that will be -- complete all the supporting material. And I suppose, Your Honour, that the next order of business would be recalendaring any motions on the amended indictment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Are there any matters that Defence counsel would like to raise at this stage?

utterances.speaker: MR. OLUJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. I should like to refer to the observation made by my learned colleague with respect to the supporting material received. The OTP has been very considerate and has sent us supporting material upon which it bases its case, Prosecution case. To the present day, we received eight large bundles with about 5 to 10.000 pieces of paper to them, and today my learned colleague says that he will be handing over some more supporting material today, which I'll be happy to receive. However, I should like to address the Chamber because we have a very great problem, and the problem is with respect to signature. The archives of the secret service of the Republic of Croatia has distributed all the documentation into 10.126 boxes, or registry boxes, and in those boxes there are 10 to 20 million papers, Your Honours. In other words, the OTP, with the material that it has given us, has not told us the addressees and the receivers, although on some of the stickers that does exist. But they haven't told us how they arrived at those materials, how they came by them. And the labels are not the kind that we need to have for us to go to the Croatian state archives and be able to control the source and authenticity of the documents themselves. In other words, I have to check out some of the documents given to me by the OTP. So I should like to ask the OTP, in a reasonable period of time necessary to get that done, to give us the correct designations so that we could check them out, as I have said. That is what I wanted to bring to the Court's attention this afternoon. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I'm surprised to hear that there is such a huge amount of documents available from the security service of the Republic of Croatia. Maybe, Mr. Scott, you could make some clarification on this issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honour, this microphone is in a bad place. It's all right now. Thanks. Mr. President, I have to say, and it's not really a complaint, counsel has been completely courteous up to the present time, and I think we've had professional dealings with each other, and so this is not in the form of a complaint, but this is the first I've heard of these concerns. I would be happy to discuss them with counsel and perhaps what would be most helpful would be if counsel could transmit to us a letter indicating his concerns with a listing of the documents that he's concerned about. I just simply don't know which documents he's referring to. I would be surprised, as Your Honour apparently is, that there is that volume, but I don't -- it's possible. I just simply don't have the information right now to make a further response. But I would be happy to receive a letter from counsel indicating his concerns and listing the documents. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, is it possible, after this sitting, the parties will meet with each other to discuss this matter?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I'm happy to talk to counsel and see if we can find a time while he is still in The Hague. I apologise, Your Honour, I'm on a very tight schedule this afternoon on another matter, so today it might not be possible but it may be possible to meet with him tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Is there anything else, Mr. Olujic?

utterances.speaker: MR. OLUJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour, nothing else. I have just heard that my learned colleague has other business to attend to today and hasn't got time for a meeting, but if there is goodwill on the part of the OTP, I will set all I have said out in writing chronologically, and I hope that the misunderstanding with respect to establishing the truth before this Court of law will be able to be resolved on a collegial basis, without any problems.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Are there any other matters that Mr. Rajic would like to raise to this Bench?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: How about the conditions in the Detention Unit? Do you have anything to complain?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. You may sit down.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I think that's all for this hearing if there's nothing else that the parties would like to bring to the attention of this Bench. The hearing is adjourned.
